subject: comb jelly
title: This Sea Creature Grows a New Anus Every Time It Poops, Then Erases It

scenes.text: This animal has no anus. Until it needs one.
The warty comb jelly. A see-through blob with rows of beating hairs that flash rainbow colours.
Biologists assumed it had a normal exit. In 2019 one scientist watched for ten days. There was nothing there.
Then waste built up, pushed the gut against the skin from inside, and the two fused. An opening popped out like a chimney.
The waste went out. The hole sealed and vanished. The babies do this about every ten minutes.
Comb jellies may be the oldest branch of complex animals alive. So this disappearing door might be how every anus began. Including yours.

description:
The warty comb jelly has no permanent anus. Marine Biological Laboratory scientist Sidney Tamm found in 2019 that the opening forms only when waste fills the gut and presses the gut wall into the outer skin; the two fuse, the waste passes, and the pore seals and disappears.
Young comb jellies repeat this roughly every ten minutes. Comb jellies are thought to be among the oldest lineages of complex animals, so the transient anus may show how the through-gut first evolved (Invertebrate Biology, 2019).

first_comment: Comb jellies are not jellyfish; they swim with eight rows of beating hairs instead of pulsing. A cousin, the sea gooseberry, has two anuses, and nobody has yet checked whether those vanish too. Which weird body part should we cover next?
